summary: M. N. Srinivas (1916–1999) worked in Indology and other fields. He studied at Elphinstone College, University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye, and University of Oxford. He held posts at Baroda College, University of Delhi, and founded and chaired ISEC.

M. R. Raghava Varier (born 1936) is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Calicut and later served there as Reader in Epigraphy from circa 1974 to 1996.

M. S. Nagaraja Rao (1932–2011) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Mysore (circa 1951–1955) and served as Director of the Department of Archaeology, Museums and Heritage from circa 1972 to 1983.

M. Seshagiri Sastri worked in Indology and linguistics. In 1899, he was attested as Curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library and Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Presidency University, Kolkata.
M. Shinoda (born 1977) is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. Shinoda studied at Agoura High School and the Art Center College of Design, and was taught by Seiren Matsunami.

Mabel Haynes Bode (1864–1922) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied at UCL and completed a PhD at the University of Bern under Eduard Müller-Hess. She held posts at UCL (circa 1912–1917) and SOAS (circa 1917–1922).

Madan Mohan Malaviya (1861–1946) was an Indology scholar who founded Banaras Hindu University. He completed his studies at the University of Calcutta (circa 1879–1884) and the University of Allahabad (circa 1889–1893).

Madeleine Biardeau (1922–2010) was an Indologist and scholar of philosophy and religious studies. After studying at the École normale supérieure de jeunes filles (~1941–1945), she served as an enseignante at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1956–1989).
Madhav Krishna Sharma was an Indology scholar who studied under C. Kunhan Raja. In 1952, he served as an Inspector for the Department of Sanskrit Education, Rajasthan.
Madhav M. Deshpande (born 1946) is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as a Professor at the University of Michigan, with posts attested in 1976 and from 2006 to 2009.
Madhu Khanna is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. In 2012, she held posts at Jamia Millia Islamia and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.

Madhukar Anant Mehendale (1918–2020) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Joint Secretary of the Linguistic Society of India in 1955 and was a Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1970, 1983).

Madhusudan Dhaky (1927–2016) was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. He studied at Fergusson College (~1947–1951) and later served at the American Institute of Indian Studies, including as Associate Director (~1976–1996, also attested 2012).

Mae Chee Huynh Kim Lan is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies from Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, where she was advised by Phra Suthithammanuwat and Veerachart Nimanong (attested 2010).

Mahesh A. Deokar is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He has held positions at Savitribai Phule Pune University, where he is attested as Professor in 2011 and as Head in 2020–2021.

Maheshachandra Nyayaratna Bhattacharyya (1836–1906) worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Edward Byles Cowell and served as Principal of the Sanskrit College and University, an affiliation attested in 1882 and 1914.

Mahinda Deegalle (born 1961) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Harvard Divinity School and the University of Chicago, holding posts at Harvard, Bath Spa University (~2001), and Colgate University (~2012–2013).

Maho Iuchi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at Otani University by 2008. In 2010, Iuchi held a post as a guest researcher at Kobe City University of Foreign Studies.
Mai Mishiro is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She held positions at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (attested 2011) and Waseda University (attested 2016).

Makio Takemura (born 1948) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1967–1975). He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Mie, Rissho, Tsukuba (~1988–2006), and Toyo (~2006–2021).
